recipes.title: Japanese pork nikujaga, light
recipes.summary: A lighter Japanese pork and potato braise with carrots, green beans and a savoury soy, rice-wine and ginger broth.

steps.instruction: Prepare the pork loin, potato, onion, carrot, green beans, ginger and spring onions in their listed forms.
Stir the soy sauce, rice wine, brown sugar and vegetable broth together.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide saucepan over medium-high heat.
Brown the pork loin until lightly coloured at the edges.
Cook the onion and carrot until the onion begins to soften.
Add the potato to the saucepan.
Pour the soy and vegetable broth mixture over the pork and vegetables.
Simmer the covered nikujaga until the potato and carrot are nearly tender.
Add the green beans and ginger to the braise.
Simmer uncovered until the green beans are tender and the broth lightly coats the ingredients.
Finish the Japanese pork nikujaga with the spring onions.
Rest the nikujaga so the savoury broth settles.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat gently until the pork and potatoes are steaming. Freeze for up to 2 months, though the potatoes will soften.

recipes.title: Korean beef patties with rice, light
recipes.summary: Tender Korean-style beef patties glazed with soy, rice wine, ginger and sesame, served with cucumber and a modest portion of rice.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender and fully steamed.
Prepare the cucumber, onion, spring onions, garlic and ginger in their listed forms.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan until fragrant.
Stir the soy sauce, rice wine, brown sugar and sesame oil together.
Mix the ground beef with the onion, spring onions, garlic, ginger, half the soy mixture and half the sesame seeds.
Shape the ground beef mixture into eight flat oval patties.
Rest the beef patties so they firm slightly.
Cook the first sides of the patties until deeply browned.
Turn the beef patties carefully.
Cook the second sides until the patties are nearly cooked through.
Brush the patties with the remaining soy mixture.
Cook until the glaze is glossy and the beef patties are fully cooked.
Finish the Korean beef patties with the remaining sesame seeds.
Serve the beef patties with the white rice and cucumber.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate the patties and rice separately for up to 3 days. Reheat the patties gently in a covered pan. Freeze cooked patties for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Thai chicken pad see ew, light
recipes.summary: A lighter Thai stir-fry of rice noodles, chicken, eggs, broccoli and mushrooms in a savoury soy and fish-sauce glaze.

steps.instruction: Prepare the chicken thigh, broccoli, mushrooms, spring onions and garlic in their listed forms.
Stir the soy sauce, fish sauce and brown sugar together.
Cook the rice noodles until flexible but still slightly firm.
Rinse the rice noodles briefly under cool water and drain them thoroughly.
Heat half the vegetable oil in a large wok or frying pan.
Brown the chicken thigh until nearly cooked through.
Transfer the chicken thigh to a clean plate.
Heat the remaining vegetable oil in the pan.
Cook the broccoli and mushrooms until tender and lightly browned.
Stir the garlic into the vegetables until fragrant.
Push the vegetables to the side of the pan.
Scramble the eggs in the cleared space until softly set.
Return the chicken thigh to the pan.
Add the rice noodles to the chicken and vegetables.
Pour the soy and fish sauce mixture over the noodles.
Toss the pad see ew until the noodles are glossy and the chicken is fully cooked.
Finish the Thai chicken pad see ew with the spring onions.

recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten freshly cooked. Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat quickly in a hot pan with a splash of water. Freezing is not recommended.

recipes.title: Turkish meatballs and potatoes, light
recipes.summary: A lighter Turkish tray of cumin-spiced beef meatballs, potatoes and peppers baked in a rich tomato sauce.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 210°C.
Prepare the potato, bell pepper, onion, garlic and bread in their listed forms.
Pulse the bread in a food processor until coarse crumbs form.
Mix the ground beef, onion, garlic, bread crumbs, eggs, cumin, paprika and half the salt.
Shape the ground beef mixture into small oval meatballs.
Coat the potato and bell pepper with the olive oil and remaining salt.
Roast the potato and bell pepper until lightly browned and nearly tender.
Stir the tomatoes, canned, tomato paste and vegetable broth into a smooth sauce.
Arrange the meatballs between the roasted potato and bell pepper.
Pour the tomato sauce evenly over the meatballs and vegetables.
Bake until the meatballs are cooked through and the sauce is bubbling.
Rest the Turkish meatballs and potatoes so the sauce settles.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat covered until steaming. Freeze the cooked meatballs, potatoes and sauce for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Vietnamese grilled pork noodle bowls, light
recipes.summary: A lighter Vietnamese noodle bowl with grilled pork loin, a little pork belly, crisp vegetables and a bright fish-sauce and lime dressing.

steps.instruction: Prepare the pork loin, pork belly, cucumber, carrot, bean sprouts, spring onions, cilantro and garlic in their listed forms.
Stir the fish sauce, lime, brown sugar, garlic and vegetable oil into a dressing.
Coat the pork loin and pork belly with one third of the dressing.
Marinate the pork loin and pork belly in the refrigerator.
Cook the rice noodles until tender but still springy.
Rinse the rice noodles under cold water and drain them thoroughly.
Heat the grill until very hot.
Grill the pork loin until browned and cooked through.
Grill the pork belly until browned and lightly crisp at the edges.
Rest the grilled pork so the juices settle.
Divide the rice noodles between serving bowls.
Arrange the cucumber, carrot and bean sprouts over the noodles.
Top the bowls with the pork loin and pork belly.
Finish the Vietnamese grilled pork noodle bowls with the spring onions and cilantro.
Spoon the remaining fish sauce dressing over the bowls.

recipes.storageNotes: Best assembled fresh. Refrigerate the pork, noodles, vegetables and dressing separately for up to 2 days. Freezing is not recommended.
